evidence.excerpt: A two-dimensional transient finite-element model of heat transfer from flat seal jaws through a multilayer OPP/tie/mLLDPE film stack was developed and validated against thermocouple measurements embedded in films at 0.1 s time resolution. Film layer thermal conductivities were taken from the literature (mLLDPE: 0.35 W/m·K; OPP: 0.22 W/m·K); jaw face temperature was set to experimentally measured values between 110 and 135 °C. Model predictions of seal-interface temperature matched experimental values with a mean absolute error of 1.8 °C across 48 test conditions. Simulations were then used to assess how jaw pressure (0.1–0.5 N/mm²) and dwell time (0.2–0.8 s) influence the time spent above the seal-initiation temperature of 97 °C at the film interface. Results show that for jaw temperatures at or below 115 °C, reducing dwell time below 0.35 s prevents the interface from reaching SIT even at maximum jaw pressure. The model provides a practical tool for setting sealing parameters without exhaustive trial runs.
